source.title_on_document: Inspiration booster or creative fixation? The dual mechanisms of LLMs in shaping individual creativity in tasks of different complexity

supplement.where: Online supplementary material at https://doi.org/10.1057/s41599-025-05867-9 (p. 10, Additional information); data at https://osf.io/9ckra/
supplement.holds: Supplementary Figs. S1-S4 (collaboration system screens); Tables S1-S4 (LLM and human idea pools); Tables S5-S6 (demographics by condition, the only likely source of per-cell sample sizes); Section S5 (procedure details); Tables S7-S8 (regressions behind the moderated mediation models)

paper_design_summary: Two online experiments with 204 participants each, run on the authors' own collaboration system. In Experiment 1 participants were randomly assigned in a 2 x 2 between-participants design to a simple task (alternate uses for a tire) or a complex task (feature ideas and solutions for VR glasses), and to a scripted partner that posted either ERNIE Bot-generated ideas (LLM partner) or human-generated ideas typed in by a research assistant (human partner); Experiment 2 crossed the same two tasks with an LLM partner that posted 10 ideas per response (batch) or 2 ideas per response (constrained), 30 ideas in total. Two experts rated each participant's ideas for creativity (novelty and usefulness, 1-5) and for creative fixation (similarity to the LLM ideas, 0-2).

eligibility.reason: Both experiments randomly assign individuals online (p. 4 and p. 5). Experiment 1 compares a scripted partner posting ERNIE Bot-generated ideas with a scripted human partner (ai_vs_active); Experiment 2 compares two LLM output configurations (ai_design). Each analyzes 204 people (Figs. 2 and 4). Experts rate the creativity of each participant's ideas. Caveat: the 'LLM partner' is a scripted feed of pre-generated ERNIE Bot ideas, not a live model the participant could prompt, so the AI role is ideas_supplied.

one_line_finding: In Experiment 1 (N = 204), expert-rated creativity was higher with an LLM partner than a human partner overall (2.45 vs 2.311, P = 0.032), higher in the simple task (2.549 vs 2.182) and lower in the complex task (2.351 vs 2.441); in Experiment 2 (N = 204), constraining LLM output raised creativity in the complex task (2.520 vs 2.139) and lowered it in the simple task (2.171 vs 2.466) (pp. 5-7, Figs. 2 and 4).
open_questions: Per-cell and per-arm sample sizes are not in the main text; Supplementary Tables S5 and S6 (demographics by condition) may give them.
Experiment 1 complex-task contrast prints F1,200 = 1.021 with P = 0.028; an F of 1.021 on (1, 200) df implies P near 0.31, so one of the two is wrong (p. 5).

Experiment 1 cell s.d. values (0.62, 0.63) exceed the pooled arm s.d. values (0.469, 0.453); Experiment 2 cell 's.d.' values (0.047, 0.048) look like standard errors. The standardizer needs checking against the OSF data.
Experiment 1 pooled contrast: d = -0.301 and 95% CI (-0.266, -0.012) appear to refer to human minus LLM; the CI looks like a CI of the raw mean difference, not of d.
Experiment 2 text calls the index of moderated mediation for fixation 'significant and positive' but prints the Experiment 1 value (-0.319, CI -0.551 to -0.118) (p. 7).
Creative fixation is defined as similarity 'to the ideas already generated by LLM'; how it was scored in the human-partner arm of Experiment 1 is not stated.
Whether participants were told the LLM partner was scripted, and whether the human partner posted the same number of ideas (30) as the LLM partner, is not stated (p. 3-4).
Whether the Experiment 2 participants are different people from Experiment 1 is not stated.
notes: Main text only; supplement not in this PDF. No diversity-across-people outcome, so across_people is not addressed despite the paper's discussion of homogenization (p. 8 calls creative fixation 'homogenization at the individual level'). The self-minus-expert creativity gap in Experiment 1 (M_human = 1.569, s.d. = 0.899 vs M_LLM = 0.954, s.d. = 0.868; t202 = 4.972; P < 0.001; d = -0.696; 95% CI (0.371, 0.859), p. 5) is not listed as an outcome because it mixes self-report with the expert score. Idea pools were matched on rated creativity (LLM vs human pools, simple: 2.160 vs 2.200, t98 = 0.516, P = 0.607; complex: 2.200 vs 2.180, t98 = -0.252, P = 0.801; p. 4). Ethics approval 1 March 2025; consent process began 29 May 2024 (p. 10). Fig. 2 legend on the PDF labels the lines Human partner and LLM partner; the plotted means agree with the printed cell means.
